sample_unit: chatbot first responses (40 scenarios x 4 chatbots)

links.outcome: Chatbot advice concordance with expert benchmark and coded safety concerns in orthodontic treatment-direction scenarios
links.effect: Exact concordance was 82.5% ChatGPT, 67.5% Claude, 42.5% Copilot, 37.5% Gemini; coded safety-concern rates ranged from 15.0% to 62.5%; chatbots gave appliance-direction advice.
links.quote: Coded safety-concern rates ranged from 15.0% to 62.5%.

links.outcome: Concordance with expert coding including 'examination required' or specialist evaluation required categories
links.effect: Exact concordance under majority benchmark was 82.5%, 67.5%, 42.5%, and 37.5% for ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini; alternative reference attenuated to 57.5%, 52.5%, 52.5%, 42.5%.
links.quote: Under the majority benchmark, exact concordance was 82.5% for ChatGPT, 67.5% for Claude, 42.5% for Copilot, and 37.5% for Gemini (Cochran Q = 34.105, p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Chatbot performance on Turkish-language patient-oriented scenarios
links.effect: Performance in Turkish varied widely across chatbots (37.5% to 82.5% concordance); single-language design limits conclusions on non-English performance.
links.quote: Under the tested single-date, single-language, and single-run conditions, the findings represent a conditional snapshot rather than a time-invariant ranking of model capability.

screen.reason: Empirical scenario-based study testing multiple consumer-facing LLM chatbots on orthodontic advice against expert consensus and assessing safety concerns, but it does not test a specific deployment safeguard or intervention.
